01 · From comparison to construction

Follow one wearer
through a day and a ceremony.

Part III established the more open body: bare chests, short layers, wraps and exposed limbs outside formal ceremony. This pass develops three school families through adult character studies, with side and rear views and material details.

Temenggong

The fold

A repeatable wearing act: overlap, tie, shoulder cloth and the difference between carried duty and displayed rank.

Nine Rains

The record

Use becomes legible through narrow bands, repair stitches and parts that can be replaced.

Kora

The listening ear

Soft volume, controlled joins and an open relationship between headwear, hair and hearing.

The sheets are design proposals, not approved canon or production patterns. Generated close-ups help us inspect an idea; they do not establish knot strength, fabric performance, waterproofing or acoustic behaviour.

Each brief asks for one mature adult wearer to remain consistent across all views. Face, body and small garment details can still drift. The school-specific notes below identify what should be preserved in the next pass.

02 · Communion · detailed proposal

Sri Temenggong Institution

Cloth becomes a carried responsibility.

Keep the deliberate waist fold, narrow border, shoulder cloth and low leaf-folded headpiece. Ceremony can expand the cloth; ordinary life leaves the chest and much of the back open.

ForestQuiet goldWarm creamEarth

Image inspection / revisions to keep
Observed in this generated sheet: the sports wrap retains a long front tail, and the border remains more ornamental than the brief intended. Shorten and secure the tail in the next sports drawing. The close-up suggests an inner tie but does not provide a complete dressing sequence.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Roomy cream long-sleeved upper garment; full kain over ankle-length trousers; a restrained shoulder drape; low leaf-folded headpiece; removable sandals.

Everyday

Bare chest, knee-length folded kain over divided shorts, a cloth carried on one shoulder and a low tied hair band. The shoulder cloth should end visibly rather than becoming a rear shirt.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and a short, securely managed hip wrap over divided shorts. No shoulder drape or trailing tie. Bare feet belong to this clean-floor footwork study.

Light field service

Bare chest, compact wrap, secured shoulder cloth and a small pouch for light stewardship. Foot and shin coverage follows the terrain and work.

Read the side and rear.

Check how the waist fold crosses the hip, how the shoulder cloth hangs down one side of the back, and whether a raised arm pulls at the waist.

A worldbuilding tension.

The earlier writing both rejects displayed rank and allows responsibility to be read in the border. For this pass I would make the readable difference a temporary duty, returned afterward, rather than a permanent trophy.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Waist fold and inner tie

The proposed overlap needs a repeatable tying sequence, enough adjustment and a way to resist loosening when sitting.

A stable-looking illustration is not a proof that a knot will hold.

Detail 02

Narrow woven border

A quiet border can identify the entrusted cloth without covering the garment in ornament. Repair and wear should remain possible.

The geometric marks are invented proposals; no historical motif meaning is being asserted.

Detail 03

Leaf-fold headpiece

A modest rise comes from folded cloth. The knot, internal support and hair attachment need to be visible in a detailed pattern study.

It should fold down for storage and remain comfortable when the wearer turns.

Next movement study: Kneel, sit on the floor, step high, raise both arms, remove sandals and refold the wrap. Observe the same adult garment on different waist and hip proportions.

03 · Reciprocity · detailed proposal

House of Nine Rains

A garment records its use without becoming a billboard.

Keep the narrow record band, plain work cloth, contrasting repairs and repairable woven headwear. The daily torso stays open; formal dress adds the tunic and mantle.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Plain undyed tunic and loose trousers, a rectangular short mantle, narrow record band, and a shallow open-weave ceremonial canopy.

Everyday

Bare chest, narrow record band, divided work shorts, visible repairs, grippy shoes and a woven sunhat. The record must remain attached without spreading into a large sash.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and secure opaque knee-length swim shorts. Put the shoulder band, packet and hat ashore. The identifier reduces to a small waistband marking.

Light field service

Bare chest, anchored record band, reinforced shorts and a compact tool belt for light monitoring. Terrain-specific footwear is part of the task.

Read the side and rear.

Check the shoulder-to-waist route across the otherwise bare back, the exact anchor point and whether the packet swings. Keep repairs in the same locations across views.

A worldbuilding tension.

The older heavy-cotton work tunic survives as a task or ceremonial layer. The new daily proposal moves durable cotton toward lower garments and tool-bearing pieces. Material weight still needs measurement in wet conditions.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Band and repairable anchor

The band can join a cloth waist tab through a small loop rather than permanent stitching across a larger garment.

The grid is a fictional record system; its encoding has not been designed or validated.

Detail 02

Contrasting stitched patch

A repair should have a visible damaged area, a patch overlap and a stitch path that can be worked again.

Printed patch graphics and clean rectangles alone do not explain a repair.

Detail 03

Replaceable hat edge

A replaceable woven edge segment connects to the ribs through accessible lacing, so damage need not discard the whole hat.

An open canopy is not automatically waterproof. Drainage, shading and wind behaviour need physical tests.

Next movement study: Squat, reach to measure water, carry a small packet, wet and dry the band, remove and replace a hat segment, and inspect how a repair behaves after repeated movement.

04 · Third Voice · detailed proposal

Kora House

Expression can be deliberate without announcing every movement.

Keep matte softness, one exposed shoulder, quiet-looking joins and an open relationship between headwear, hair and ears. Colour remains a wearer choice; this plum family is one sample.

01 · Formal / clothed02 · Everyday / open03 · Movement / secure04 · Field / task-led
Formal ceremony

Long pleated wrap-coat and inner layers, sculpted soft shoulder volume, flat quiet shoes and a soft head roll that sits clear of the ears.

Everyday

Bare chest and one soft drape over one shoulder, with substantial pleated divided lower wear. The waist join should hold the cloth without creating a full poncho.

Sport / movement

Bare chest and soft pleated divided training shorts; no shoulder cloth or headwear. Bare feet are shown for the clean-floor breath-and-movement study.

Light field service

Bare chest, compact shoulder cloth tied clear, soft lower layers, cloth pockets and task-appropriate quiet footwear. Observation and mediation are the proposed roles.

Read the side and rear.

Check the exposed back, the one-sided shoulder panel, a stable waist join and ear clearance when the head turns. The garment should not become a different wrap in every view.

A worldbuilding tension.

A single uniform colour or silhouette would work against the earlier freedom of colour and acoustic specification. Treat this as one approved construction family among several, subject to actual sound testing.

Three construction questions

Detail 01

Head roll, ear and hair

The soft head structure can sit behind the ear while leaving room for curls or other hair forms. Attachment must not rely on one haircut.

This is a design option, not a restriction on personal or religious head coverings.

Detail 02

Cloth-loop fastening

A sewn fabric loop and a short controlled tail can reduce loose hard components. The join should be reachable by the wearer.

Soft-looking does not establish silence, strength or ease of dressing.

Detail 03

Pleat and folded seam

Pleats give the lower garment movement without a long trailing layer. A folded seam can contain loose edges.

Only material samples and movement tests can establish what sound the cloth actually makes.

Next movement study: Turn the head, raise an arm, sit, gesture and walk over timber and stone. Compare cloth sound and sole sound separately, and keep deliberate audible signalling available.

05 · What the pictures cannot decide

Keep the tests specific.

QuestionNext evidenceDecision it would support
Can this be put on?Numbered dressing sequence, reachable joins and a temporary cloth mock-up on more than one body.Whether a wearer can dress independently and retain the same silhouette.
Can it move?Side and rear movement drawings, seated poses, raised arms and a short material trial.Where a wrap needs a shorter hem, an anchor or a different fold.
Can it be maintained?Repair access, repeated fastening, laundering and wet/dry handling.Whether the design carries its own philosophy through ordinary use.
Does it do what it claims?Band legibility and attachment tests; headwear fit and drainage; separate cloth and shoe sound observations.Which evocative details can become credible garment mechanisms.
Does identity survive?Match face, body, fastening side, patch positions, headwear and hem length across views.Which generated details to retain, redraw or discard.

No numerical performance rating is assigned here. A quiet-looking seam, a knotted fold or an open canopy is a visual proposal until its behaviour has been observed.

06 · A portable review record

Keep what works.
Name what needs redrawing.

Write a note per school and export the record. Browser storage is used when available. No choice here changes the fictional canon or the live website.

07 · Provenance and scope

Three studies
within a seven-school world.

This volume follows the adult open-body direction established in Dress Atlas III. Earlier historical analogues remain in Part I; the A/B construction workshop remains in Part II.

All detailed cuts, joins, colour families and headwear mechanisms shown here remain proposals. The three character sheets were made with the built-in image-generation tool using the Part III everyday and headwear sheets as references. Exact prompts are included in the image package.

The package contains original PNG and JPEG copies, the standalone HTML and development notes. Image sizes are reported as generated; JPEG export changes the file format, not the design or pixel dimensions. The HTML embeds viewing copies and includes a larger on-screen viewer. No website has been edited.
